THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 153

Reverend Lewis Holland was vice-president and partner with Professor Halsell in the early College, and was born November 8, 1840, in Maury County, Tennessee, and died in that state in 1815 after reaching maturity moved to Illinois, and some time later to Arkansas, where he died in 1837. His wife was a widow (ill), whose maiden name was Leah Alls, the second, in 1868, at Brandtline, of an elder partner was the second.

In 1861 Lewis Holland enlisted in Company D, Fourteenth Arkansas Confederate Infantry, and went with his command to Perryville. He came to Texas. He surrendered. Afterward he came to Texas at Ladonia, on the road to Bonham. He was a teacher in the Methodist Church, and also taught school. He later taught at Ladonia, at Ladonia, and at Ladonia. He later taught in more private school at Camp Bowie[?], where some of his students went. He received experience in the Methodist Church, with which church he was connected for many years, and to which denomination he has devoted most of his life, interested in the interests of the Church and widely known as the Savoy Star.

August 31, 1875, Mr. Holland married Mrs. Nancy M. Scott, daughter of the Rev. H. P. Scott of White County[?], Tennessee. To this union were born several children. The college records the singular fact that 'all five of the children were educated at Savoy and that Dade is on a five year schedule.' Mr. Holland also published the Baptist News and became a Baptist, to which denomination he made many contributions to its many years in the interests of the Church and widely known as the interests of the Church and widely known as the Savoy Star.

${ }^{1}$Biographical Souvenir of The State of Texas, 1889, pp. 119, 122. Brenham, Texas.
${ }^{2}$Personal letter from J. H. Holland to the author, Savoy, Texas, July 15, 1938.
